from parse import parse_line
from clean import clean_title
from money import parse_salary
from rules import keep
from pipeline import run


def test_parse_salary():
    """Test that parse_salary correctly handles spaces as thousands separators"""
    # Should handle single space (like 1200 000)
    assert parse_salary('1200 000') == 1200000
    # Should handle double spaces (like 1 200 000)
    assert parse_salary('1 200 000') == 1200000
    # Should handle no spaces
    assert parse_salary('1200000') == 1200000
    print("✓ parse_salary tests passed")


def test_keep_includes_equal():
    """Test that keep includes jobs with salary equal to minimum"""
    jobs = [
        {'id': '1', 'title': 'Job1', 'salary': 1000000},
        {'id': '2', 'title': 'Job2', 'salary': 50000},  # equal to minimum
        {'id': '3', 'title': 'Job3', 'salary': 30000},
    ]
    result = keep(jobs, 50000)
    assert len(result) == 2
    assert any(j['id'] == '2' for j in result)
    print("✓ keep includes equal salary tests passed")


def test_pipeline_with_spaces():
    """Test that the pipeline correctly processes salaries with spaces"""
    lines = [
        '1;Software Engineer;1 200 000',
        '2;Data Analyst;1200 000',
        '3;Intern;30000',
    ]
    result = run(lines, 50000)
    assert len(result) == 2
    # Should include jobs with salary >= 50000
    titles = {j['title'] for j in result}
    assert 'Software Engineer' in titles
    assert 'Data Analyst' in titles
    print("✓ pipeline with spaces tests passed")


def test_pipeline_with_equal_min():
    """Test that jobs with salary equal to minimum are kept"""
    lines = [
        '1;Job with min salary;50000',
        '2;Job above min;100000',
    ]
    result = run(lines, 50000)
    assert len(result) == 2
    print("✓ pipeline with equal minimum tests passed")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_parse_salary()
    test_keep_includes_equal()
    test_pipeline_with_spaces()
    test_pipeline_with_equal_min()
    print("\n✓ All tests passed!")"}}}]
